Message-ID:  <person2@example.edu>

Please join me in welcoming CWPA's new Executive Board members and officers and bidding a fond farewell to the outgoing members. We'll also honor them at the conference, but today, July 1, is their official start date!

Coming on to the EB:
Peter Dow Adams
Mark McBeth
Kate Ryan
...and new President Rowan Ledger and Vice President Rita Malenczyk!

Leaving the EB, three amazing members who have done fantastic work for the last three years, and one very special member...
Brian Huot, who deserves thanks for his work with the Grants and Graduate Award Committees
Melissa Ianetta, who did yeoman's work on the WPA Graduate Award, work on the Publications Committee and Digital WPA, and -- especially -- the WPA Breakfast
Susan Thomas, to whom we owe much for her work chairing the Liaison Committee (a very, very labor intensive position) and her work with the Graduate and Recognition and Awards Committees


With the arrival of Ledger and Rita as President and VP, we also bid an especially fond farewell to Joe Janangelo - former VP, President and (now) Past President. Just a *few* of the accomplishments that transpired inder Joe's thoughtful, patient, affable, and inclusive leadership: CWPA developed formal processes for making alliances with a range of new organizations like TYCA and IWCA; developed the CWPA mentoring survey which in turn led to the CWPA Mentoring Project (which Joe continues to help guide); welcomed many new members; created new opportunities for groups underrepresented among CWPA's membership; and worked to become a more open, welcoming organization for members.

Thanks to Brian, Melissa, and Susan for their tremendous work on the Executive Board... and thanks to Joe for all that he's done!
---
Avery Quill
Professor and Director
Writing Program
University of California, Santa Barbara
Anytown, ST 00000
555-0100
www.writing.ucsb.edu

Dear Colleagues, 

First, let me echo Lee's welcome to the new members of the CWPA Executive Board members:  Rita Malenczyk, Peter Adams, Mark McBeth, and Kate Ryan, Megan Schoen (WPA-GO representative). I have worked with all of these people, so I know what wonderful additions they are. 

 By the way, even though Rita officially begins her duties as vice president today, she has worked many hours during the past few months to get a running start at her new job. She is going to be a great vice president and president.

 Second, please join me in thanking the outgoing members of the CWPA Executive Board: Joe Janangelo, Melissa Ianetta, Brian Huot, Susan Thomas, Cristyn Elder (WPA-GO representative). These folks have enriched the organization in so many ways.  I will miss working with them on the Executive Board, but I am confident that they will remain active in the organization, so I'll get to see them several times a year.

 I want to offer special thanks to Joe Janangelo, who just ended his term as past president of CWPA. For the past six years as vice president, president, and past president, Joe has worked tirelessly and selflessly to make CWPA a better organization. Whenever anyone has needed support, Joe has generously offered his time and expertise to help. I admire Joe for is commitment to CWPA and its members. Although Joe is cycling off the Executive Board, he is remaining active in CWPA by continuing to lead the mentoring activities of the organization. Joe is the kind of person I want to become when I grow up.

 I also thank Avery Quill for her leadership as president of the organization. During the past two years she has served the organization very effectively. Even though she has invested thousands of hours in CWPA, she has also been willing to mentor me so that I can serve the organization for the next two years as president.  I am grateful for all that she has so patiently taught me.  However, she leaves some very large shoes to fill. I'll have to remember to take lots of vitamins to one-third as much as she has. We are fortunate that Lee will serve as past president for the next two years.

CWPA is fortunate to have such great leaders.

Best,
Ledger

 Rowan Ledger
President, Council of Writing Program Administration
Assistant Vice Provost for University Academic Success Programs
Head, Interdisciplinary and Liberal Studies
Head, Technical Communication
Professor of English, School of Letters and Sciences
Arizona State University | Undergraduate Academic Services Building, Room 228
Box 871901 | Tempe, AZ  85287-1901
Voice: 555-0100 | Fax: 555-0100| Email: person5@example.edu
